claims.claim: **Manage a burn as trauma**, prioritising burns first aid. **Accurate TBSA drives the fluid decision — and TBSA excludes epidermal burns.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Primary survey first — do not get distracted by the burn.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Airway burn/inhalation signs** — hoarseness · stridor · respiratory distress · black sputum · facial swelling · singed nasal hairs · soot in the mouth, intraoral oedema, significant neck burn: **consider early intubation.** Suspected airway burn or carbon monoxide: **high-flow oxygen.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Full-thickness or circumferential chest/abdominal wall burns with abnormal breathing: consider escharotomy** — needs the tertiary burns service.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Early shock — look for a cause other than the burn.** Ideally 2 points of IV/IO access; bolus for haemodynamic instability; **IV fluid if over 10% TBSA**, rate by the modified Parkland formula.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Take off any clothing, nappy or jewellery** touching the burn or lying distal to it. **Cool under cool running water as soon as possible (within 3 hours), 20 minutes in total.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Never apply ice; avoid hydrogel burn products.** Cooling may be paused for hypothermia or significant distress.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Cling film lengthways — never wrapped circumferentially, and not on the face or a chemical burn.** Paraffin ointment for facial burns.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Prevent hypothermia:** remove wet clothes and dressings after cooling, cover the wound and child, warm the room or use warming devices, consider warm IV fluids.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Chemical burns: discuss decontamination with Poisons Information, 131126.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consider child abuse:** immersion scalds, patterned contact burns, a mechanism that does not fit the pattern, burns on the back or genitalia. Check tetanus status.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Analgesia early and throughout, especially for dressings and mobilisation. For debridement and dressing changes, procedural sedation is recommended.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Over the first 48–72 hours, depth is hard to judge.** Erythema-only (epidermal) areas are left out of the estimate.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Depth by appearance:** epidermal — red, no blisters, brisk refill, sensation present · superficial dermal — pale pink, blisters, brisk, painful · mid dermal — dark pink, blisters, sluggish, ± sensation · deep dermal — blotchy red, ± blisters, refill and sensation absent · full thickness — white, no blisters, refill and sensation absent.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Baseline tests:** major burn (≥10% TBSA) — Hb, electrolytes, BGL, group and hold, VBG · suspected inhalation — VBG for CO or cyanide · electrical — ECG.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Count from the time of the burn, not presentation.** Resuscitation fluid is **Hartmann's**, with maintenance **sodium chloride 0.9% + glucose 5% through a separate line**; volume by the Modified Parkland Formula.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Give half in the first 8 hours, the rest over the next 16.** Review the rate every 1–2 hours against urine output and fluid state — the total is an estimate. **Hartmann's is first choice; sodium chloride 0.9% if unavailable.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Urinary catheter; nil by mouth with a nasogastric tube** (risk of ileus). Delayed resuscitation, electrical and inhalation injury need more fluid — discuss with the specialist team.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **De-roof blisters over 5 mm or crossing a joint.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Facial burns: fluorescein 2% for corneal damage.** Ocular burns: irrigate with sodium chloride 0.9% for 30 minutes or more, topical chloramphenicol, **urgent ophthalmology review.** Alkali eye injury may need 2–4 hours of irrigation — continue until the pain settles and the eye pH reads 7.0–7.2.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Suspected carbon monoxide or cyanide poisoning: 100% oxygen**, and liaise early with the burns unit, ICU and Poisons Information.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Electrical injury:** involve the burns service and ICU early; look for entry/exit wounds; consider spinal precautions and **24-hour ECG monitoring**; monitor CK and urine haemoglobin.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Discuss with the state paediatric burns service** for: over 5% TBSA · over 5% full thickness · a special area (face, ears, eyes, neck, hands, feet, perineum, genitalia or a major joint) even if under 5% · any inhalation injury · circumferential · chemical or electrical · associated trauma or spinal injury · **under 12 months** · suspected abuse.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Involve the local paediatric team** for suspected abuse · a self-inflicted burn · multiple co-morbidities · doubt about caring for the burn at home.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23
